rows.en:
(Huh... A paper airplane...
Did it come flying down from the roof...?)
Okay, I'll go check it out!
Yo, \p.
I knew it was you, Alto.
'Knew it'? What's that supposed to mean?

I saw a paper airplane flying, so I figured
I'd find you if I went up to the roof.
So that's why...
Your paper airplanes sure fly well, Alto.

That's what you get after tweaking them
over and over.
Teach me how to make them!
No way.
Cheapskate.
rows.notes: Insult as a bare epithet, as in the Japanese.

rows.en: Call me whatever you want.
Total cheapskate! Long-hair! Indecisive wimp!
rows.notes: Three insults (super-stingy, long-haired, indecisive); 'wimp' added to make the third land as an insult.

rows.en: ...You really had to go that far?

You're the one who said I could call you
whatever I want!
...Sheesh...

Then how about this: if I win a paper airplane
showdown, you teach me how.
Fine, you're on.
Not that it matters. I'm the one who's gonna win.
I'm not gonna lose!
(What kind of paper airplane should I make?)
Focus on design
Go for simplicity
Imitate Alto's
If it looks cool, it'll fly!
You sure about that?
rows.notes: x6 across the three choice branches.

rows.en:
With this, I'm gonna... beat your paper airplane,
Alto!
rows.notes: Japanese names Alto in third person (declaration); made it 'your ... Alto' since he is right there.

rows.en: Then let's settle this.
I lost...
I win.

I'm not saying going for design is bad, but if
you want it to fly, you've gotta stick to the basics.

Get the balance between the body and the main
wings right, and even that one'll fly as well as mine.
rows.notes: Shujiku (main axis) rendered 'body' of the plane.

rows.en: I built mine strictly by the book!

I'm not saying sticking to the basics is bad, but
if you want it to fly farther, give it some flair.

Try going bold and making the main wings bigger,
and even that one'll fly as well as mine.

I snuck a peek at how Alto folds his
and used it as a reference...

Copying mine isn't gonna let you
beat the original.

You're on the right track. Work on it a bit more,
and even that one'll fly as well as mine.
Got it, thanks.

Well, see ya.
Let's fly 'em again sometime.
(Alto grumbles a lot, but he's a good guy.)
I knew it was you, Saotome-kun.

Hey, your paper airplanes sure fly well,
Saotome-kun.

You're the one who said I could call you
whatever I want!
I'm not gonna lose, so there!
Imitate Saotome-kun's

With this, I'm gonna... beat your paper airplane,
Saotome-kun!
I built mine totally by the book!

I snuck a peek at how Saotome-kun folds his
and used it as a reference...
(Saotome-kun grumbles a lot, but he's a nice person.)
(School's out, huh... I'm beat again today.)

\p,
let's head home.
Yeah, fine by me, but...
But are you sure?
What are you talking about?
Behind you, behind you.
Huh?
Ranka, what are you doing... over there...?
...And Sheryl too...?
Do you need something?
I thought I'd walk home with you, Alto-kun.

I was just going to do my servant Alto the favor
of letting him come shopping with me.
Well, well...
Wh-what...?

I figured Michel was the only one girls chase,
but you're no slouch either, Alto.
rows.notes: Sumi ni okenai = you're quite something / dark horse.

rows.en:
Shut up!
It's not like that...
Hold on, you. Aren't you getting the wrong idea?

Alto and I don't have that kind of relationship.
Don't say weird things.
Oh, okay, sorry...
As long as you understand.
Sheryl-san...
rows.notes: Also spoken by the female player in Sheryl scenes.

rows.en: So, which one are you going with?
Alto-kun...
Alto? You know what to do, don't you?
Ugh...

Guess this is what they call a love-triangle
showdown.

\p...
We're making a run for it.
Huh? Why?
